title: Molech
lead: Molech is the name, or perhaps the kind of offering, linked in the Bible with "making children pass" through fire, a practice the law forbids (Leviticus 18:21; 20:1–5) and the prophets condemn at Jerusalem's Valley of Hinnom (Jeremiah 7:31; 32:35).

sections.b: The Torah forbids handing children over to Molech (Leviticus 18:21; 20:2–5; Deuteronomy 18:10). Solomon built a shrine for Molech, "the vile idol of the Ammonites" (1 Kings 11:7), and kings Ahaz and Manasseh made their sons pass through the fire (2 Kings 16:3; 21:6). Josiah defiled Topheth in the Valley of Hinnom so that no one could do it again (2 Kings 23:10). Jeremiah says this was something God "did not order," which "never even crossed my mind" (Jeremiah 7:31; 19:5; 32:35). The valley's name, Ge-Hinnom, became Gehenna, the New Testament word for hell (Mark 9:43–48). Scholars debate whether Molech was a god (John Day, George Heider) or a type of sacrifice (Otto Eissfeldt). They also debate whether the children were killed, as Ezekiel 16:20–21, Ezekiel 23:37–39 and Psalm 106:37–38 say of the rites in their day, or dedicated by passing through fire, as the rabbis held (Mishnah Sanhedrin 7:7).
